action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
### Reasoning
The current board state shows an empty top four rows, with O in row 4, column 3, and X in row 5, column 3. This means X played first in the center (column 3), and O stacked on top. It's now X's second turn.

The goal is to make the optimal move, which in early-game Connect 4 means positioning to build towards winning lines while controlling key areas, preferably creating connected structures.

Playing in column 3 would place another X at row 3, column 3, resulting in X (row 5), O (row 4), X (row 3) in the center column. However, these X's are separated by O and do not form a connected 2-in-a-row (not consecutive vertically).

Instead, playing in an adjacent column (2 or 4) places the new X at row 5, creating a horizontal 2-in-a-row at the bottom with the existing X in column 3. This builds a connected structure, which is better for progressing towards 4-in-a-row than isolated pieces.

Columns 2 and 4 are symmetrically equivalent due to the board's symmetry around column 3. Among equivalent optimal moves, I select the smaller column index (2) as the tiebreaker convention.

This move controls central bottom positions and sets up potential extensions horizontally, vertically, or diagonally, while O has no immediate threat.

Final Answer: 2

X controls the very bottom of the center but is blocked from building upward there by the existing O. The highest-value response is therefore to claim the same central file for O and begin building upward from the existing O piece. Dropping in column 3 immediately creates a vertical 2-in-a-row for O directly in the middle of the board (the strongest single structure available on this turn). Vertical center control is a well-known Connect-4 priority because it simultaneously supports multiple diagonal, horizontal, and additional vertical threats on future plies while denying the same to X. Adjacent options (column 2 for a horizontal 2, or column 4 for a diagonal 2 plus bottom-center occupation) are reasonable but inferior; they either shift play away from the absolute center or create a less-flexible connection.

This move maximizes long-term forcing opportunities and board control.
